summary: Iteration 166, backend only. Tested the whole-page low-res validation in tejas_core.validate_crop_pages and the Pillow PNG compress_level=6 change for reviewed full-res images. All runs were in the foreground, in-process ASGI on the preview pod, using disposable isolated Mongo DBs (dropped afterwards) and the original local PDF bytes behind a mocked storage GET. No live calls, no customer-DB writes, no object-store PUTs, no app code changes. CORRECTNESS: 100/100 tests passed. All 19 papers validated: every ref goes through _crop_geometry, and exactly one whole-page 0.3 raster is made per referenced page (Jan24S1 201 refs/26 pages, Apr08S2 199/25). No PNG encode and no _render_crop_png call in preflight. Every fail-closed case raises and caches no proof. Rotated pages, thin regions and annotations accept nothing the old clip path rejected. Delivered full-res crops are pixel-identical to pre-163 on all 400 refs. PERFORMANCE: cold preflight Jan 4689 -> 1131/1136 ms (4.1x faster), Apr 9134 -> 330/328 ms (27.7x faster); warm unchanged, 1 coalesced source GET. TRADE-OFFS: (a) PNG6 costs a lot of CPU on the largest scanned Jan images: about +31% CPU per cold image and +37% for the remaining-images-sequential run, for 19% fewer bytes. On Apr it saves only 0.3% bytes and 90/199 images get larger. (b) During a cold Jan preflight, one unrelated /api/series request took about 1.03 s, up from 0.73/0.20 s in iter163/164. It happened in both runs, though each run had only 2 probe samples. Likely cause: each whole-page get_pixmap holds the GIL about 43 ms instead of about 24 ms per clip. Live deployer 520 is still UNRESOLVED (independent platform problem, not retested). Performance is NOT qualified for 500k users or global 4G.

minor.issue: Material CPU regression on the largest scanned images: Jan encode CPU +77%, about +31% CPU per image end to end, and +37% for remaining-images-sequential (10.8 -> 14.7 s CPU per paper per pod), for -19% bytes. On Apr it saves only 0.3% bytes and makes 90/199 PNGs larger. Pixels and dimensions are unchanged.

A whole-page get_pixmap holds the GIL about 43 ms per page on Jan scanned pages, versus about 24 ms per old clip. One /api/series probe took about 1.03 s, versus 0.2-0.73 s before, but the whole stall window shrank from 4.7 s to 1.1 s. Apr got better (GIL hold 9 ms vs 53 ms).

A non-int page fails with a non-ValueError: page '2' or None gives TypeError (from sorting or the arithmetic), page 1.0 gives an AssertionError from PyMuPDF. It still fails closed, but it would surface as a 500 if refs were not validated upstream. Curated refs are int.

Actual behaviour: old clip and new whole-page validation BOTH ACCEPT truncated or garbage DCT streams. MuPDF only warns ('padding truncated image') in both, so neither path rejects corrupt images. This is parity, not a regression.

action_items: Decide whether to keep PNG compress_level=6 for every reviewed full-res crop. It costs +31% CPU per cold Jan image for -19% bytes, and gives almost no byte saving on Apr. Options: gate it by pixel count or source type (scanned large pages only), or benchmark compress_level 1-3. Derivatives are cached, so this mainly hurts cold or evicted pods.

Optional: whole-page raster holds the GIL about 43 ms per Jan page. If tail latency of co-located requests during a cold preflight matters, move validation to a process pool. Splitting into clip bands would bring back the per-clip image decode cost.
Optional hardening: coerce or validate ref['page'] as int before sorting, so bad refs map to ValueError/4xx and not a TypeError/AssertionError 500.
Optional cleanup: the _display_lists parameter of _render_crop_png is now dead in production (only exercised by tests).
Live 520 is still UNRESOLVED (independent platform/deployer problem); not retested here.
critical_code_review_comments: validate_crop_pages: each ref runs through _crop_geometry (page range, rect containment, omit containment) before the raster check. Refs are sorted by page and fail on the first bad ref. The proof is cached only after full success (validation:2 key). The doc is closed via the context manager. Correct.

The renderable-pixel check (rect*0.3).irect.is_empty is geometric. A sweep of thin/zero-pixel rects at 4 rotations found no case accepted by new but rejected by the old clip path. The old path actually raised FzErrorArgument (not ValueError) for zero-width clips, so the new ValueError is cleaner.
The whole-page get_pixmap check proves only that the page renders at 0.3, not that every image decodes. Same as before: MuPDF pads corrupt JPEGs.
Delivery path is unchanged apart from the PNG encoder. The 400-ref pixel comparison against pre-163 passed (same RGB and dimensions).
